commit_message:
QUIC: 0RTT for gnutls via CURLSSLOPT_EARLYDATA

When a QUIC TLS session announced early data support and
'CURLSSLOPT_EARLYDATA' is set for the transfer, send initial request and
body (up to the 128k we buffer) as 0RTT when curl is built with
ngtcp2+gnutls.

QUIC 0RTT needs not only the TLS session but the QUIC transport
paramters as well. Store those and the earlydata max value together with
the session in the cache.

Add test case for h3 use of this. Enable quic early data in nghttpx for
testing.

Closes #15667

+                         unsigned char *quic_tp, size_t quic_tp_len,
+                         struct Curl_ssl_session **psession);
+

fix_commit_message:
vtls_scache: fix race condition

- Lock before counting the cache sessions.

Prior to this change when taking a session a trace command counted the
sessions but not under lock, which caused a race condition.

Reported by: Viktor Szakats

Fixes https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/18806
Closes https://github.com/curl/curl/pull/18813
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 2a25ebe9580e on top of intro 68bd759c2bfe via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (DataRace): Curl_ssl_scache_take() in lib/vtls/vtls_scache.c releases the SSL session cache mutex (Curl_ssl_scache_unlock) before it finishes reading shared state protected by that lock: specifically, the trace/log statement calls Curl_llist_count(&peer->sessions) to report the remaining number of cached sessions for the peer, but this call happens after the unlock. Any other thread sharing the same Curl_easy handle's session cache (multi-threaded libcurl usage sharing a share object / connection cache) can concurrently modify peer->sessions (or even free the peer) between the unlock and the count read, causing a race condition on the linked list. Root cause: When Curl_ssl_scache_take() was reworked to add QUIC 0RTT support and richer trace logging, the call to Curl_ssl_scache_unlock(data) was placed immediately after the critical section that removes/takes a session from the peer's session list, but before the subsequent trace-logging code that itself reads the same shared peer->sessions list (via Curl_llist_count) to report the remaining session count. This left a window where lock-protected data is read/used without holding the lock.
